report.title: Inside The Server: 14 Months of Offensive Cyber Operations Targeting Europe

candidates.evidence_excerpt: 46.8.236.121 | Threat Actor server with exposed open directory

DarkLunnen used a modified proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit developed by watchTowr for FortiGate CVE-2024-55591, designed to create a backdoor super-admin account named “service”. The operator identified approximately 600 vulnerable devices in Turkey, 16 in Ukraine, 14 in Azerbaijan, and 1 in Algeria.

The operator scanned 12,183 Ukrainian and Polish IPs for Hikvision cameras vulnerable to CVE-2017-7921 and identified eight vulnerable devices. The findings indicate attempted targeting but do not confirm that the cameras were compromised.

Shell command history revealed additional apparent operations, including Exchange webshells, a possible compromise of a German network involving stolen NTLM hash, S3 backup access, exploiting attempts involving Roundcube CVE-2025-49113, a Czech organization backup archive.

Enable private data encryption. It ships off by default, and while off, FortiOS protects stored secrets such as VPN passwords with the system default key, so anyone holding the config can decrypt them offline (the origin of CVE-2019-6693).

Disable LLMNR and NBT-NS, require SMB signing, block outbound SMB (TCP 445) at the perimeter, and patch CVE-2025-24071. The operator kept Responder and its capture database on the server, along with a proof of concept for CVE-2025-24071, which leaks NTLM hashes when a user extracts a crafted archive
